AdjustHoldingsInput.description:
Adjusts many Holdings in one commit, e.g. a night of memory decay. How much
anything decays is the client's policy.

on.description: Positions of the generated event on additional axes.

AdjustHoldingsInput.title: AdjustHoldingsInput

At.description:
A read position. `tick` is on the main axis unless `axis` names an
additional axis (`axis.define`); then it is a position on that axis.

axis.description: An additional axis to read on. Absent: the main axis.

AxisDef.description:
An additional order of time, such as reading order next to story order.
The main axis (`Position.tick`) is implicit and has no definition.

BatchTransitionStatus.description:
The statuses `transition.batch` applies. `superseded` is not one of them:
it needs a replacement record, which `holding.adjustBatch` writes.
BatchTransitionStatus.title: BatchTransitionStatus

BeliefAboutItem.description:
What a holder thinks another holder knows (`umwelt:holds` Holdings), next
to what the other holder actually holds at the same position.

actuallyHolds.description: Whether the other holder really holds the claim (active, available).

polarity.description: True: the holder thinks the other holds the claim. False: thinks not.

BeliefAboutItem.title: BeliefAboutItem

Breach.description: A secret told to someone outside its circle.

recordId.description: The recipient's Holding acquired by being told.

Breach.title: Breach

CanonStatus.description: How a claim relates to canon at the read position.
CanonStatus.title: CanonStatus

CheckUtteranceInput.description:
Claims a holder says or thinks, to check against what the holder can know.
The claims come from the client (or a model it runs): the engine never
reads free text.
CheckUtteranceInput.title: CheckUtteranceInput

consistent.description: Every claim has the verdict `holds` with the same polarity.

ClaimKeyResult.description: The keys the engine derives from a claim (`spec/claim-key.md`).

claimKey.description: Identifies the claim whatever its polarity.

ClaimKeyResult.title: ClaimKeyResult

timelineId.description: Timeline to write to; defaults to "main".

ContextAdmitInput.description:
Decides which candidates may enter a context seen from one perspective.
Without `holder` the perspective is the narrator's, who sees everything
visible at the position.

includeWithheld.description:
Admit suppressed and inaccessible Holdings. Requires
`authorizedNarrator`.

ContextAdmitInput.title: ContextAdmitInput

admitted.description: Admitted candidates, highest priority first (ties keep input order).

ContextCandidate.description:
Something a client wants to put in a context (a prompt, a scene brief).
Exactly one of `recordId` and `eventId` is given.

cost.description: Budget units the candidate costs (tokens, lines...). Defaults to 1.

id.description: The client's own id for the candidate.

priority.description: Higher priorities are admitted first when the budget is short.

ContextCandidate.title: ContextCandidate

ContextRejection.description:
Why a candidate was refused. Checks run in this order and a candidate
reports the first one it fails.

oneOf.description: No such record or event in this project and timeline.

Read on an additional axis, and the candidate's event has no position
on it: it is visible to nobody there.
Retracted, revoked, forgotten, abandoned or superseded.
Not part of the holder's perspective.
Suppressed or inaccessible for the holder.
The same record or event was already admitted.
Higher-priority candidates used the budget first.

ContextRejection.title: ContextRejection

EmbeddingDocRef.description:
A searchable document: a record (a Fact, or a Holding with text) or an
event whose type does not begin with `umwelt:`.

textHash.description: The `textHash` the vector was made from (see `embedding.pending`).

EmbeddingSpace.description:
The vectors of one embedding model. A vector is only compared with
vectors of the same space. `model` documents the model; the engine never
reads it and never runs a model.

EnsureEntityInput.description:
One entity owned by another system (a game, a wiki, a host app), keyed by
its `externalRef`. Ensuring it twice is a no-op; changed fields are updated.

id.description: Id used only when the entity is created; an existing entity keeps its id.

EnsureEntityInput.title: EnsureEntityInput

EnsureWorldInput.description:
A manifest of what must exist: the project and its entity types, entities,
predicates and axes. Ensuring it creates what is missing, in one
transaction, and leaves what is already there untouched; anything that
exists with another definition refuses the whole manifest.
EnsureWorldInput.title: EnsureWorldInput

EntityAtResult.description:
An entity as canon describes it at one position: its current name, title
and aliases from `umwelt:name`, `umwelt:title` and `umwelt:alias` Facts,
falling back to the entity's own name and aliases.

recordIds.description: The Facts the name, title and aliases come from.

EntityAtResult.title: EntityAtResult

EntityKnownResult.description:
An entity as one holder knows it: only what the holder's own active,
available Holdings say. A holder that knows no name gets none.

aware.description: The holder has an Awareness record of the entity.

recordIds.description: The Holdings the name, title and aliases come from.

EntityKnownResult.title: EntityKnownResult

on.description:
Positions on additional axes. Records and transitions of the event
inherit them.

groupHolding.description: The group's own Holding, if the group itself holds the claim.

missing.description: Members holding nothing about the claim.

HoldingAdjustment.description:
A new value for an active Holding. The old Holding is superseded by a copy
carrying the changed fields; its history stays readable.

newRecordId.description: Id of the replacing Holding. Generated when absent.

HoldingAdjustment.title: HoldingAdjustment

HoldsAs.description:
Whether the Holding behind a `holds` answer has the polarity that was
asked about. A holder who believes the opposite still holds the claim.

oneOf.description: The Holding has the polarity of the claim asked about.
The Holding has the opposite polarity: the holder holds the negation.

HoldsAs.title: HoldsAs

holds.description: The holder has a Holding about the claim, with either polarity.

holdsAs.description:
Whether that Holding affirms what was asked (`same`) or its negation
(`opposite`). Absent when `holds` is false or the question gave only
a `claimKey`, which has no polarity.

baseTimelineId.description: Timeline to branch from: "main" (the default) or an active draft.

operationIndex.description: Index in the proposal: records first, then transitions.

stale.description: A vector exists but was made from another text.

text.description: The text the search indexes for this document: embed exactly this.

textHash.description: SHA-256 of `text`, to send back with the vector.

PendingEmbeddingsInput.description:
Documents visible in a timeline whose vector in a space is missing or
stale, with the text to embed.
PendingEmbeddingsInput.title: PendingEmbeddingsInput

nextCursor.description: More pending documents follow; pass it as `page.cursor`.

resumeCursor.description:
Where a later call can start to see only documents written after this
one. Starting without a cursor checks every document again.

ProposalRebaseResult.description: A pending proposal checked again against the current head of its timeline.
ProposalRebaseResult.title: ProposalRebaseResult

timelineId.description: Timeline to write to; defaults to "main".

PutEmbeddingsInput.description: Stores or replaces vectors in one transaction.
PutEmbeddingsInput.title: PutEmbeddingsInput

stale.description:
Stored vectors whose `textHash` is not the document's: they stay
pending until replaced.

secrecy.description: The holder keeps this secret; only `sharedWith` may be told.

position.description: Omitted: the position of the commit's event.

provenance.description: Omitted: the provenance of the commit's event.

position.description: Omitted: the position of the commit's event.

provenance.description: Omitted: the provenance of the commit's event.

secrecy.description: The holder keeps this secret; only `sharedWith` may be told.

position.description: Omitted: the position of the commit's event.

provenance.description: Omitted: the provenance of the commit's event.

position.description: Omitted: the position of the commit's event.

provenance.description: Omitted: the provenance of the commit's event.

position.description: Omitted: the position of the commit's event.

provenance.description: Omitted: the provenance of the commit's event.

score.description:
The value the item was ranked by: the cosine similarity in a semantic
search, the fused rank score in a hybrid one. Absent in a text search.

SearchSemantic.description:
The semantic part of a search: a query vector made by the client's model
in one of the project's embedding spaces.
SearchSemantic.title: SearchSemantic

Secrecy.description:
Marks a Holding as a secret. The engine never blocks telling it: telling
anyone outside `sharedWith` (besides the holder) is recorded and reported
as a breach.

SetDispositionsInput.description:
Records many Disposition values in one commit (trust, affection...). The
newest value per holder, target and dimension is the current one.

on.description: Positions of the generated event on additional axes.

SetDispositionsInput.title: SetDispositionsInput

Timeline.description:
A line of history. "main" is the confirmed history of a project; a draft
branches from its parent (main or another draft) at `baseVersion` and is
later promoted into that parent or discarded.

baseVersion.description: Head version of the parent when the draft was opened. Absent for main.

depth.description:
Drafts from main down to this timeline: 0 for main, 1 for a draft of
main, at most `MAX_DRAFT_DEPTH`.

parentTimelineId.description:
Timeline this draft branched from: "main" or another draft. Absent for
main.

Timeline.title: Timeline

TransitionBatchInput.description:
One status change applied to many records in one commit, e.g. everything a
character forgets overnight. `superseded` needs a replacement and is not
accepted here; use `holding.adjustBatch`.

on.description: Positions of the generated event on additional axes.

TransitionBatchInput.title: TransitionBatchInput

position.description: Omitted: the position of the commit's event.

provenance.description: Omitted: the provenance of the commit's event.

TransmitBatchItem.description:
One transmit of a batch: a `TransmitInput` whose shareable fields may be
left to the batch's `shared`.
TransmitBatchItem.title: TransmitBatchItem

on.description: Positions of the generated event on additional axes.

timelineId.description: Timeline to write to; defaults to "main".

TransmitShared.description:
What every transmit of a batch has in common, written once. A field given
by an item wins over the shared one.
TransmitShared.title: TransmitShared

recordId.description: The Holding that decides the verdict.

UtteranceVerdict.description: How a claim relates to what the holder holds at the read position.

oneOf.description: The holder holds the claim with the opposite polarity.
The holder holds another value in the same functional slot.
The holder holds it, but suppressed or inaccessible.

The holder only comes to hold it at a later tick (on the read's axis):
an anachronism.
Nothing the holder holds covers the claim.

UtteranceVerdict.title: UtteranceVerdict

memberOf.description:
Only holders that are members of this group at the read position
(an active `umwelt:member-of` Fact).

recordIds.description: One Holding id per claim, in claim order. Empty: generated.

WitnessInput.description:
One event seen by several holders: every witness gets a `witnessed`
Holding for every claim, in one atomic commit. Who saw what, and how
clearly, is the client's decision.
WitnessInput.title: WitnessInput

WitnessedClaim.description: One claim seen at a witnessed event.

canon.description: Also record the claim as canon (a Fact) in the same commit.

WitnessedClaim.title: WitnessedClaim

WorldCreated.description: What a manifest created; everything else was already there.

WorldDivergence.description: One thing a manifest asks for that already exists with another definition.

field.description: The field whose stored value differs.

WorldDivergence.title: WorldDivergence

WorldProject.description:
The project of a world manifest. Unlike `project.create`, the id is
required: it is what makes the manifest repeatable.
